newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says '96 car sales to match '95.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says '96 car sales to match '95.

text.p: Volvo Car's sales volumes were lower in the third quarter of 1996 than in the corresponding period a year ago but year-on-year sales were level, the company said on Wednesday.
Order volumes in the third quarter were also down, Volvo Car's managing director Tuve Johannesson told a news conference after the release of the company's nine-month results.
"In the third quarter car volumes were lower than in the same period of 1995," Johannesson said.
"The volumes for our order book have throughout 1996 stayed at the same level as 1995. Our sales for the full year this year will be at the level of 1995."
This means the company will sell about 374,000 cars and produce about 370,000 cars, a fall from earlier estimates.
In June, Johannesson forecast production this year would reach at least 380,000 cars.
Johannesson stressed that Volvo's models were in the main selling according to plan with the exception of the luxury 900 series, whose sales have this year fallen by 26 percent.
Johannesson said this was due to a weak market and this segment had been troublesome in all countries, not only in Sweden but also in Thailand and Taiwan.
He said the new coupe model C70 showed that Volvo Car can work with external partners.
The company thrives on different types of cooperation, said Johannesson, pointing at joint ventures with Mitsubishi.

"We work together in production at NedCar (in The Netherlands) and will soon also on engines. Mitsubishi's GDI-motor (Gasoline Direct Injection) will be offered as an alternative in the S40/V40 and we estimate that it will move between 15,000 and 30,000 motors a year," he said.
Volvo Car on Wednesday posted a drop in operating profit to 573 million crowns in the nine months ending September 30 from 1.93 billion a year ago.
The unit reported sales volumes slipping five percent to 59.83 billion crowns.
